value.name: sends pointed text to Rosa
value.description: Asha sends Rosa a direct question about what the staff said regarding the fall, avoiding any softening.
evidence: thumbed out the question she had been avoiding by not answering: What did the staff say about the fall. She sent it without softening it

value.name: receives evasive reply from Rosa
value.description: Rosa replies with a caring but nonresponsive message, choosing not to answer the question directly.
evidence: The reply that came was not the one she had asked for—Thinking of you. Call me whenever.—and she read it twice, understanding that Rosa had chosen, deliberately, to answer the person before the question.

value.name: decides against texting further
value.description: Asha puts the phone down and resolves not to text again until she is ready for a phone call.
evidence: She set the phone down face up beside the laptop and did not text again, because the next thing she said would have to be on a phone call, and she was not ready yet to hear the details in someone's voice.

value.name: puts on shoes slowly
value.description: Asha sits down and slowly works her feet into her shoes, delaying the departure.
evidence: Asha sat on the kitchen chair beside the bag and worked her feet into her shoes one at a time, slower than the task asked for.

value.name: resists calling Rosa
value.description: Asha hesitates over the phone, knowing a call would force her to hear about the fall before leaving home.
evidence: listening to herself almost reach for the phone and not quite do it.
Calling Rosa now would mean hearing the word fall in someone else's mouth, in the kitchen, before she had even left the house, and she was not willing to start the trip there.

value.name: leaves phone behind and departs
value.description: Asha picks up her bag and leaves the phone on the counter as she heads out.
evidence: She straightened, picked up the bag by its strap, and left the phone where it was.
